items.title: Henry A. "Hank" Kmen Interview, 1963-02-13
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] And my name is Dick Allen. ... [INTERVIEWEE] What does he go back to, Dick, about the 1890s?

ctx.x: I think we'll skip over your career as a musician if you don't mind for the time being. Not at all. And, uh, go on to, uh, your scholarly endeavors. What you think, uh, you've seen. I'll let you take over and discuss it and make my end of it as vague as possible.

Well, this will have to be very general. But, uh, anybody who wants to support the generalities, but particulars, will be able to find evidences here in the written material, at least some of the stuff I've done. Uh, one thing that I believe is easily proved is that New Orleans was a unique city in a very real sense. Different from any other American city, where the other American cities all much more like each other than any of them were like New Orleans. And I think this uniqueness, uh, as much as anything,…
Well, what about the rest of the country, as compared with New Orleans, as far as general musical sophistication is concerned? Both Negro and white, I'm talking about.
